structured_output.summary: I added a run-collapse fast path in GroupedAggregateHashTable::AddChunk, in src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp only, with no header change. It runs after TryAddCompressedGroups and before the normal hash path. When every group column is fixed-width (TypeIsConstantSize) and there are at most 8 columns, it looks for runs of adjacent rows with identical keys. Two rows count as equal when both are NULL or both are valid with the same bytes (memcmp). If more than n/2 rows start a run, it bails out to the normal path. Otherwise it slices the run heads into dict_state.unique_values, hashes them, calls FindOrCreateGroups on the heads only, gives every row its run head's address and calls UpdateAggregates. It built cleanly and the bench checks passed. Measured: the subquery HASH_GROUP_BY CPU time went from 6.48s to 5.62s in the profile, but q18 wall time only moved 635->629 ms (-0.9%) in one run and 630->612 ms (-2.8%) in another. Both are inside the ~5% noise band and below the acceptance bar, so I am abandoning it.
structured_output.generality: This would apply to any hash GROUP BY on fixed-width keys whose input is clustered or sorted on the key, such as runs of rows sharing a parent key, time series grouped by id, or the output of a sort. It does not apply to variable-width keys, to unclustered input (where it bails out after one pass comparing adjacent rows), or to inputs that already take the dictionary or constant paths.
structured_output.notes: Cutting the probes by about 4x (only ~25% of rows are run heads on q18) does not change wall time much for a 15M-group aggregate. Hashing, probing and matching are not the bottleneck. The cost is most likely in creating and materialising 15M groups into the TupleDataCollection and in partition finalize/combine, which run collapse cannot touch. Follow-up for q18: get a breakdown of sink vs finalize for this aggregate and target the group materialisation or finalize/combine, for example a perfect-hash/direct-indexed aggregate for dense integer keys, like the q13 large perfect HA. The code is small and correct, so it could be revived later as a cheap helper for low-cardinality clustered aggregates, but by itself it has no measurable effect on q18.
